[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Columbia, South Carolina facility (DartPoints own internal code CAE01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 1000 Catawba St Suite 180, Columbia, SC 29201, within the South Carolina Research Authority (SCRA) Innovation Center, positioning it centrally for statewide reach across South Carolina per the operators own description.

reading.body:
DartPoints Columbia publishes 2 MW of IT capacity, making it the only facility in South Carolina with a disclosed megawatt figure, though this reflects a data gap rather than a capacity lead since 13 other mapped facilities publish no load figures.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 2 MW represents roughly 50 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a typical colocation density, it represents roughly 200 racks. Either scaling places this as a small facility. No published data covers redundancy tier, power utilization effectiveness, or cooling architecture, so the suitability of the physical infrastructure for sustained GPU workloads cannot be assessed from what DartPoints discloses.

For AI infrastructure deployment, 2 MW sits below the threshold at which hyperscale or frontier-model training campuses are typically measured. No published specifications confirm the power density, redundancy, or connectivity needed for large accelerator workloads. The facility could support inference or smaller training clusters, but no operator disclosure confirms either use case. A reader serious about deploying AI infrastructure here would need to request specifications absent from the published page.
